STYLE: Documentary illustration for a history film. Medium: painterly realism fused with a hand-tinted 19th-century engraving; fine cross-hatching and subtle paper grain; warm sepia and umber palette with deep black shadows, small touches of muted gold and restrained deep red. Setting: Zululand, southern Africa, January 1879: rolling green-gold grassland, rocky ridges, scattered thorn trees, and the steep isolated rocky hill of Isandlwana shaped like a crouching sphinx. Historical accuracy: Zulu warriors of 1879 wear simple war dress (loin covers of fur strips, a few with cow-tail ornaments or headbands, older married men with a dark headring), carry tall oval cowhide shields in matching regimental hide colours, short broad-bladed stabbing spears and some old muzzle-loading guns; no feather headdresses, no film costume. British soldiers of 1879 wear red tunics, dark trousers, white foreign-service helmets and carry long rifles; tents are white bell tents; transport is ox-wagons. Constraints: no text, no lettering, no flags or banners, no logos, no watermark; every human figure anonymous (seen from behind, in silhouette, in shadow or at a distance, no identifiable faces); no blood, no gore, no bodies. Widescreen 16:9 cinematic composition.
Z01: The steep rocky hill of Isandlwana under a heavy, darkening sky; an empty grass plain in front of it, wind moving through the grass, long cloud shadows. No people. Silent, mournful.
Z02: The hill of Isandlwana at dusk, a dark silhouette against a fading gold sky, long golden grass in the foreground, a few thorn trees. No people. Quiet, final.
Z03: A Zulu regiment assembling on a grassy hillside at morning: hundreds of men seen from behind and at a distance, tall oval cowhide shields of matching dark hide held upright, short spears, dust in the low sun.
Z04: Close detail: a man's hand gripping a short broad-bladed stabbing spear held against a tall oval cowhide shield; an old muzzle-loading musket leans nearby on the grass. Only hands, shield and weapons in frame, no face.
Z05: Zulu warriors running at speed across open grassland in loose open order, shields carried at their sides, dust kicked up, seen from the side at a distance; a sense of speed and discipline.
Z06: Long columns of Zulu warriors marching across vast rolling grassland hills, tiny in the frame, winding over the folds of the land under a wide sky; a huge landscape.
Z07: Two older Zulu commanders with dark headrings and cloaks, seen from behind on a rocky rise, watching regiments gather in the wide valley below.
Z08: A British military camp in 1879: rows of white bell tents spread across the slope at the foot of the steep rocky hill of Isandlwana, ox-wagons parked between them, thin smoke from cooking fires, soldiers small in the distance.
Z09: Two British soldiers in red tunics and white helmets seen from behind on the edge of a tented camp, one looking through field glasses across an empty sunlit grass plain towards distant hills.
Z10: Small groups of Zulu warriors moving quickly and low through tall grass along the folds of a valley, shields held close, using the ground to stay hidden, seen from a distance.
Z11: Looking down from a ridge into a deep grassy valley filled with thousands of Zulu warriors sitting silently in rows with their shields, stretching far into the distance; tense stillness.
Z12: Before dawn: a column of mounted men and infantry marching out of a tented camp by lantern light, dark hills beyond, the first grey light on the horizon; seen from behind.
Z13: A half-empty British camp at mid-morning: rows of white tents and parked ox-wagons, only a few soldiers moving about, the steep rocky hill of Isandlwana above; quiet and exposed.
Z14: Night in a hidden valley: Zulu warriors resting on the grass with their shields, no fires, under a dark star-filled sky with no moon; deep blue-black shadows.
Z15: A small patrol of horsemen in colonial dress on a grassy ridge, seen from behind, reining in their horses and looking down into a valley below; midday light.
Z16: A grassy valley erupts: thousands of Zulu warriors rising to their feet at once, shields lifted, dust rising, seen from the ridge above at a distance; overwhelming motion.
Z18: A long thin line of British infantry in red tunics and white helmets, some kneeling and some standing, firing rifles across open grass; white powder smoke drifting; seen from behind and to one side.
Z19: Zulu warriors pressed flat in the long grass under fire, shields laid low, white powder smoke drifting over them; seen from a distance, no wounds shown.
Z20: One anonymous Zulu man standing upright in the open long grass with his arm raised, among many warriors lying flat; seen from behind; smoke in the air; courage.
Z21: A mass charge: a wave of Zulu warriors surging forward through powder smoke with shields up, across open grass towards a distant line; seen at a distance; overwhelming momentum.
Z22: British soldiers in red tunics falling back in disorder through smoke towards the white tents of the camp, seen from a distance; confusion.
Z23: Thick dust and smoke rolling over abandoned white tents and overturned ox-wagons beneath the rocky hill; no people visible; aftermath.
